_note: Curated condition knowledge. Used for offline scoring, follow-up questions, RAG documents, medicine candidates and diet rules. 'mild' = the natural (no-medicine) plan may be offered.

generic_questions.q: Do you have fever? If yes, how high (if measured) and since when?
Are you taking any medicines right now for this problem?
Have you had this problem before?
Has anyone around you (family, office, school) had similar symptoms recently?
How is your sleep, appetite and water intake these days?

conditions.name: Common cold (viral upper respiratory infection)

follow_up.q: Is your nasal discharge clear, or yellow/green?
Do you have fever above 101 F (38.3 C)?
Do you have any breathing difficulty or wheezing?

conditions.overview: The common cold is a viral infection of the nose and throat. It usually gets better on its own in 7-10 days.
self_care: Rest and drink plenty of warm fluids
Saline nasal drops for a blocked nose
see_doctor_if: Fever above 102 F or lasting more than 3 days
Breathing difficulty, chest pain or ear pain

conditions.name: Influenza (flu)

follow_up.q: Did the fever and body ache start suddenly?
What is your highest measured temperature?
Do you have any chronic illness such as diabetes, asthma or heart disease?

conditions.overview: Flu is a viral infection that causes sudden fever, body aches and tiredness. Most people recover in 1-2 weeks, but older adults, pregnant women and people with chronic illness can get complications.
self_care: Rest at home and avoid spreading it
Paracetamol can lower fever and ache
see_doctor_if: You are over 65, pregnant or have a chronic illness

conditions.name: Viral fever
suggested_tests: Dengue NS1 / IgM if fever > 2 days

follow_up.q: How many days have you had fever, and is it continuous or coming and going?
Do you have a rash, bleeding gums, or pain behind the eyes?
Do you have shivering with fever at fixed times?

conditions.overview: Viral fever is a general term for fever caused by a virus. It usually settles in 3-7 days. In India, dengue, malaria and typhoid must be ruled out when fever lasts more than 2-3 days.
self_care: Rest and drink 2.5-3 litres of fluids a day
Sponge with lukewarm water for high fever
Paracetamol for fever; avoid ibuprofen/aspirin until dengue is ruled out
see_doctor_if: Rash, bleeding, severe abdominal pain or vomiting

conditions.name: Dengue fever
suggested_tests: CBC with platelet count (repeat daily if low)

follow_up.q: Do you have pain behind the eyes or severe joint/muscle pain?
Any red spots on skin, bleeding gums or nose bleeds?
Is there dengue in your area or have many mosquito bites recently?

conditions.overview: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral infection common in India during and after monsoon. It causes high fever, severe body pain and can lower platelets. Warning signs usually appear when the fever goes down (days 3-7).
self_care: Drink plenty of fluids (ORS, coconut water, soups)
Daily platelet count as advised by doctor
see_doctor_if: Any bleeding, severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting
Restlessness, drowsiness or cold clammy skin

conditions.name: Malaria
suggested_tests: Peripheral blood smear for malaria parasite

follow_up.q: Does the fever come with shivering and then heavy sweating?
Have you travelled to or live in an area with malaria cases?

conditions.overview: Malaria is a parasite infection spread by mosquitoes. Fever with chills that comes in cycles is typical. It needs a blood test and prescription antimalarial treatment.
see_doctor_if: Always see a doctor for suspected malaria
Confusion, jaundice, dark urine or breathing difficulty is an emergency

conditions.name: Typhoid (enteric fever)

follow_up.q: Has the fever been rising slowly day by day for more than 5 days?
Have you eaten outside food or drunk untreated water recently?

conditions.overview: Typhoid is a bacterial infection spread through contaminated food and water. It causes prolonged fever, weakness and stomach upset and needs prescription antibiotics.
self_care: See a doctor for testing and antibiotics
see_doctor_if: Always see a doctor for suspected typhoid
Severe abdominal pain, blood in stool or confusion is an emergency

conditions.name: COVID-19

follow_up.q: Have you lost your sense of smell or taste?
Do you have a pulse oximeter? What is your oxygen level (SpO2)?

conditions.overview: COVID-19 is a viral respiratory infection. Most cases are mild, but oxygen level below 94% or breathing difficulty needs urgent care.
self_care: Check oxygen level twice a day if you have an oximeter

conditions.name: Sore throat (pharyngitis)

follow_up.q: Do you see white patches on your tonsils or have swollen neck glands?
Is there cough and runny nose along with the sore throat?

conditions.overview: Most sore throats are caused by viruses and get better in about a week. White patches with high fever and no cough may mean a bacterial (strep) infection that needs a doctor.
self_care: Warm salt-water gargles 3-4 times a day

conditions.name: Allergic rhinitis (dust/pollen allergy)

follow_up.q: Do the sneezing fits happen in the morning or around dust/pollen?
Do you have fever with it?

conditions.overview: Allergic rhinitis is an allergy to dust, pollen or pets that causes repeated sneezing, itchy and runny nose. It is not an infection and has no fever.
self_care: Wear a mask in dusty places
see_doctor_if: Symptoms affect sleep or work despite home care

conditions.name: Sinusitis

follow_up.q: Does the face or forehead pain get worse when you bend forward?
How long have you had the blocked nose?

conditions.overview: Sinusitis is swelling of the sinuses, usually after a cold. Most cases are viral and improve within 10 days.
see_doctor_if: Symptoms beyond 10 days or getting worse after improving
Swelling around the eyes or high fever

conditions.name: Asthma / wheezing

follow_up.q: Do you hear a whistling sound while breathing?
Is it worse at night, with exercise, cold air or dust?
Do you already have an inhaler prescribed?

conditions.overview: Asthma is long-term swelling of the airways causing wheezing, cough and breathlessness. It needs a doctor's inhaler plan.
self_care: Avoid smoke, dust and cold air
see_doctor_if: You need your reliever inhaler more than twice a week
Breathlessness at rest or lips turning blue (emergency)

conditions.name: Gastroenteritis / food poisoning

follow_up.q: How many loose motions or vomits in the last 24 hours?
Is there blood or mucus in the stool?
Are you passing urine normally and able to keep fluids down?

conditions.overview: Gastroenteritis is a stomach and gut infection, often from contaminated food or water. The main danger is dehydration; most cases settle in 2-3 days.
self_care: Bland food: khichdi, curd rice, banana
see_doctor_if: Blood in stool, high fever, or more than 6-8 motions a day
Not passing urine for 8 hours, very dry mouth, dizziness

conditions.name: Acidity / acid reflux (GERD)

follow_up.q: Is the burning worse after meals, spicy food or when lying down?
Do you have difficulty swallowing, weight loss or black stools?
How much tea/coffee do you drink and do you smoke?

conditions.overview: Acidity happens when stomach acid flows back into the food pipe, causing burning in the chest or upper stomach. Meal habits and stress make it worse.
self_care: Eat smaller meals, do not lie down for 2-3 hours after eating
Reduce tea, coffee, spicy and fried food
Raise the head end of the bed
see_doctor_if: Difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood or black stools
Chest pain with sweating (rule out heart problem)

conditions.name: Constipation

follow_up.q: How many times a week do you pass stool?
How much water and fruit/vegetables do you have daily?
Any blood in stool or unexplained weight loss?

conditions.overview: Constipation means hard or infrequent stools, usually from low fibre, low water or less activity.
self_care: Fibre: fruits, vegetables, whole grains, isabgol
see_doctor_if: Blood in stool or black stool
Lasts more than 3 weeks despite diet changes

conditions.name: Migraine

follow_up.q: Is the headache on one side and throbbing?
Does light or noise make it worse?
Any triggers you noticed: missed meals, less sleep, stress, screen time?

conditions.overview: Migraine is a recurring headache, often on one side with nausea and sensitivity to light. Triggers include poor sleep, skipped meals, stress and dehydration.
self_care: Rest in a dark, quiet room
see_doctor_if: Headache with fever and stiff neck

conditions.name: Tension headache

follow_up.q: Does it feel like a tight band around your head?
How many hours of screen time and sleep do you get daily?

conditions.overview: Tension headache is the most common headache, a dull pressure around the head often linked to stress, posture, screen time and poor sleep.
see_doctor_if: Headache daily for more than 2 weeks
Headache with vision changes, weakness or vomiting

conditions.name: Urinary tract infection (UTI)

follow_up.q: Do you have burning or pain while passing urine?
Any fever, back/side pain or vomiting?
Is there any chance of pregnancy?

conditions.overview: A UTI is a bacterial infection of the bladder or urinary tract, more common in women. It usually needs prescription antibiotics after a urine test.
self_care: Do not hold urine for long
See a doctor for a urine test
see_doctor_if: Fever, back pain or vomiting (kidney infection)

conditions.name: Iron-deficiency anemia

follow_up.q: Do you get tired or breathless easily on climbing stairs?
For women: are your periods heavy or longer than 7 days?
Are you vegetarian, and how often do you eat green leafy vegetables?

conditions.overview: Iron-deficiency anemia is very common in India, especially in women. Low iron reduces hemoglobin, causing tiredness, paleness and breathlessness.
self_care: Iron-rich foods with vitamin C (lemon, amla) to improve absorption
Avoid tea/coffee within 1 hour of meals
Iron tablets as advised by doctor

conditions.name: Vitamin D deficiency

follow_up.q: How much time do you spend in sunlight daily?
Do you have bone or lower back pain?

conditions.overview: Vitamin D deficiency is very common in India despite sunshine, due to indoor life and covered skin. It causes bone pain, muscle weakness and tiredness.
self_care: 15-20 minutes of sunlight on arms and face (10 am - 3 pm) most days
Vitamin D-rich foods: eggs, fish, fortified milk
Supplements only as advised by doctor

conditions.name: Vitamin B12 deficiency

follow_up.q: Do you get tingling or numbness in hands or feet?
Are you vegetarian or vegan? Do you take metformin or acidity tablets regularly?

conditions.overview: Vitamin B12 is mainly found in animal foods, so deficiency is common in vegetarians. It causes tiredness, tingling and anemia.
self_care: Milk, curd, paneer, eggs or fish daily
see_doctor_if: Numbness, balance problems or memory changes

conditions.name: Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid)

follow_up.q: Have you gained weight without eating more, or feel cold when others don't?
Anyone in your family with thyroid problems?

conditions.overview: In hypothyroidism the thyroid makes too little hormone, slowing metabolism. It is diagnosed with a TSH test and treated with daily thyroid tablets prescribed by a doctor.
self_care: Take thyroid tablet on an empty stomach if prescribed

conditions.name: Type 2 diabetes / high blood sugar

follow_up.q: Do you feel very thirsty and pass urine often, including at night?
Does anyone in your family have diabetes?
How active are you (walk/exercise minutes per day)?

conditions.overview: Type 2 diabetes means the body cannot use insulin well, so blood sugar stays high. It is very common in India and is controlled with diet, exercise and medicines prescribed by a doctor.
self_care: Avoid sugar, sweets and sugary drinks; choose whole grains
see_doctor_if: Sugar above 300 or very thirsty and drowsy (urgent)

conditions.name: High blood pressure (hypertension)

follow_up.q: Have you measured your blood pressure? What were the readings?
How much salt, pickles, papad or packaged food do you eat?

conditions.overview: High blood pressure usually has no symptoms but damages the heart, brain and kidneys over time. Readings of 140/90 or more on repeated checks need a doctor.
self_care: Less than 5 g salt a day; avoid pickles, papad, chips
see_doctor_if: BP 180/120 or more with headache, chest pain or weakness (emergency)

conditions.name: Dehydration / heat exhaustion

follow_up.q: How many glasses of water do you drink a day?
Have you been out in the heat or had vomiting/loose motions?

conditions.overview: Dehydration happens when the body loses more water and salts than it takes in, often from heat, sweating, vomiting or diarrhea.
self_care: ORS, coconut water, lemon water with salt
Avoid going out in peak afternoon heat
see_doctor_if: Confusion, fainting or very high body temperature (emergency)

conditions.name: Muscular back pain

follow_up.q: Does the pain spread down the leg, or is there numbness in the leg?
Any trouble controlling urine or stools?

conditions.overview: Most back pain comes from strained muscles or posture and improves in a few weeks with movement and simple care.
self_care: Keep moving gently; avoid long bed rest
Good posture and breaks from sitting
see_doctor_if: Pain down the leg with numbness or weakness
Pain after a fall or with fever

conditions.name: Stress / anxiety

follow_up.q: Do you feel worried or tense most days?
How many hours do you sleep, and is it disturbed?

conditions.overview: Stress and anxiety are common and can cause a racing heart, poor sleep, headaches and stomach upset. Talking to someone and daily routines help.
self_care: Deep breathing or meditation 10 minutes a day
see_doctor_if: Panic attacks or anxiety affecting daily life

conditions.name: Sleep problems (insomnia)

follow_up.q: What time do you go to bed and use your phone in bed?
Do you snore loudly or wake up choking?

conditions.overview: Insomnia is difficulty falling or staying asleep. Most cases improve with a fixed routine and less screen use at night.
self_care: Same sleep and wake time daily
see_doctor_if: Sleep problems for more than a month
